# Project Kestrel: Seller Draft Review Against Buyer Playbook

**Bottom line:** The Seller's package departs from our playbook on nearly every material point. It also presents these positions as "key negotiated" and "fair and balanced," but we have not agreed to any of them. Our response should say so expressly. Several Seller positions sit at our conditional fallbacks (20% cap, 18-month period), which we cannot concede without Amelia Frost's written approval identifying the draft, and none has been given. This is a playbook-level review for the deal team, not a substitute for NSW counsel's sign-off.

## 1. Departures from the Playbook

| Issue | Seller draft | Playbook | Gap |
|---|---|---|---|
| General cap (cl 12.1) | 20% / AUD 4.8m | 25% / AUD 6m start; 20% only as a conditional fallback with Frost's written authority | Opens at our fallback without authority |
| De minimis (cl 12.2) | AUD 25,000 | AUD 5,000 | 5x higher; small claims excluded |
| Basket (cl 12.2) | AUD 250,000, excess-only recovery | AUD 50,000, first-dollar once exceeded | 5x higher and deductible, not tipping |
| General claims period (cl 12.3/13) | 18 months | 24 months; 18 months only with Frost approval | Fallback without authority |
| Time-limit spillover | Any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated | Separate regimes; no hidden general-regime override | Would pull Title and fraud into general limits |
| Fundamental/Title | Same caps and time limits as general warranties | 100% cap, 6+ years, outside basket/de minimis/knowledge bar | Complete departure |
| Limitations/exclusive remedy/non-reliance (cl 9.3, 12.8, 20.5) | Apply to "all Claims of any nature" | Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out to the maximum enforceable extent; non-waivable | No fraud carve-out |
| Disclosure (Sch 7; DL 1.1, 1.2) | Whole data room, Accounts, statutory registers, public records | Specific fair disclosure only; reject data-room/public-register deemed disclosure | Whole-data-room disclosure |
| Buyer knowledge (cl 8.3) | Excludes anything Buyer "had knowledge" of, including data-room or public-record matters | Delete blanket exclusion; any qualifier needs named seller knowledge persons and reasonable enquiry; never excuses title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities | Blanket exclusion, no carve-outs |
| Bluefen (cl 3/6.3) | Reasonable endeavours; consent "satisfied on delivery" | Effective consent and evidence conditions satisfied before Completion | Consent-on-delivery and endeavours standard |
| Riverlark (cl 2/7) | ~AUD 3.2m; release after Completion | Current payout; direct repayment from Completion funds; effective releases; post-Completion release only with irrevocable undertaking and Frost approval | No repayment in funds flow; post-Completion release |
| DD-005 bonuses | Matter "for the Seller"; not itemised in funds flow | AUD 420k plus on-costs as a specific line item or seller-funded; not silently excluded | Silently excluded; on-costs unaddressed |
| Ironquay IP (cl 11.1) | Indemnity limited to SOW3 payment; "adequate" | Broaden the indemnity, preserving the SOW3 cure; AUD 180k unverified | Narrow indemnity |
| DD-006 export incident (cl 4.6/Sch 6) | "Preliminary operational matter," "not expected to be material" | Preserve logs, investigate, require updates; assume no confirmed breach or harm either way | Materiality opinion, no preservation or update obligations |
| Sandbar renewals (AUD 330k) | "Ordinary-course operating costs" | Assess; no automatic debt classification or price deduction | Characterisation presented as settled |
| Tax/IP | "Settled under the general regime" | OPEN; no unlimited liability assumed; no resolution assumed | Treats open items as closed |
| Title | DD-012 share register evidences title | Independent evidence of title, ownership, encumbrances and authority; DD-012 is a supplied internal source only | Relies on a seller-supplied register |

## 2. Material Issues and Reasoning

### 2.1 Limitation architecture (the most significant issue)
The Seller has stacked every limitation against us at once: a lower cap, a much higher de minimis, a deductible basket, a shorter period, and a spillover clause that applies general limits to all claims. Together these would gut the general warranty regime.

Illustration (using only the figures above):
- A AUD 20,000 claim: Playbook recovers it (above AUD 5,000 de minimis, counts toward the basket). Seller draft: recovers nothing (below AUD 25,000).
- Aggregate AUD 300,000 of valid claims: Playbook recovers the full AUD 300,000 (basket exceeded, first-dollar). Seller draft recovers AUD 50,000 (excess over AUD 250,000).

Pushback: reject all of cl 12.1–12.3 and 13 in their current form and restore the playbook numbers. Any movement on cap or period needs Frost's prior written authority identifying the specific draft. The 20%/18-month positions should not be conceded in this round.

### 2.2 Title and fundamental warranties
Putting capacity and title warranties under the general caps and time limits is the single most dangerous proposal. Title failures are typically discovered late and go to the value of the shares we are buying. "Administrative simplicity" is not a reason. Restore the separate regime: 100% cap, at least six years, outside the basket, de minimis and knowledge bar.

### 2.3 Fraud carve-out
The Seller's "all Claims of any nature" language would capture fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct. The playbook carve-out is non-negotiable and cannot be waived. Require that caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance expressly do not apply to these matters, to the maximum extent enforceable under NSW law.

### 2.4 Disclosure
The Seller's combination of cl 1.1, 1.2 and Schedule 7 would deem disclosure of the whole data room, the Accounts, statutory registers and public records. This converts our diligence into the Seller's disclosure. Require specific, fair disclosure against specific warranties. Reject deemed disclosure from data room, public registers or prudent search.

Also note the disclosure is stated as at 5.00pm on 22 September 2026. Today is 6 November 2026, so the record is about six weeks old. Require a refreshed disclosure and data-room cut-off, plus a bring-down at signing and Completion.

### 2.5 Buyer knowledge (cl 8.3)
A bar on claims for matters "discoverable from the data room or public records" effectively turns the Buyer's diligence against it. Delete the blanket exclusion. If the Seller insists on any knowledge qualifier, it must name seller knowledge persons, require reasonable enquiry, and never apply to title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities.

### 2.6 Bluefen consent (about 30% of FY26 revenue, ~AUD 3.6m)
The Seller's draft states that consent is "satisfied on delivery," that the Seller will only use reasonable endeavours, and the disclosure confirms no final written consent has been provided. A customer representing roughly 30% of revenue is material. Require effective written consent and evidence that the conditions in clause 11.3 are satisfied before Completion. Reasonable endeavours is not enough for a material customer consent. We also need to review clause 11.2/11.3 itself, which the Seller has not provided.

### 2.7 Riverlark (~AUD 3.2m)
The Seller proposes a release "following Completion," with no repayment in the funds flow and no current payout figure. The disclosure confirms the facility has not been repaid and the discharge of security is not included. Require:
- A current payout letter.
- Direct repayment from Completion funds.
- Effective security releases at Completion.

Any post-Completion release requires an irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost's approval.

### 2.8 DD-005 bonuses (AUD 420,000 plus on-costs)
The funds flow omits these bonuses. The disclosure also does not say whether payroll tax or superannuation applies. The Seller says this is "a matter for the Seller," but if the company pays them after Completion, we bear the cost. Require either a specific line item in the funds flow or seller funding. On-costs must be quantified and covered on the same basis. Do not allow the funds flow to silently exclude them.

### 2.9 Ironquay IP (DD-004 cl 7.3; DD-010 AUD 180,000)
Under DD-004 cl 7.3, SOW3 project materials transfer only once every SOW3 fee is paid. The data room has no receipt or confirmatory assignment, and the Seller calls the narrow indemnity "adequate." The AUD 180,000 should not be treated as verified either way. Broaden the indemnity to cover IP ownership and transfer defects, not just the SOW3 payment. Keep the SOW3 cure mechanism (payment, then confirmatory assignment) so the Seller can resolve it.

### 2.10 DD-006 export and privacy incident
The Seller describes this as "not expected to be material." That is an opinion, not a disclosed fact. The data shows a download link sent to an unintended external address, with up to about 1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). It is unknown whether anyone accessed the file or whether notification obligations arise under the Privacy Act 1988 (Cth). Consistent with the playbook, do not assume a confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or a numeric demand. Instead:
- Require preservation of logs.
- Require the investigation to proceed.
- Require regular written updates until the scope and any notification question are resolved.

Ask NSW/privacy counsel whether any specific protection is needed. That is a deal-team decision, not something to assume now.

### 2.11 Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000)
The Seller calls these ordinary-course costs. The disclosure says it is unknown whether each renewal is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary-course. Request the contracts and a breakdown of each renewal. Do not accept the characterisation as settled, and do not automatically treat the amount as debt or deduct it from price. Keep the question open for the debt and working capital analysis.

### 2.12 Tax and IP
The Seller calls these "settled under the general regime." They are not. Our position is that Tax and IP terms remain open, with no unlimited liability and no resolution assumed. Keep Tax, IP, payment and covenant categories separate. Do not allow the general regime to override them quietly.

### 2.13 Title evidence
The share register at DD-012 is a Seller-supplied internal document, not independent proof. Require independent evidence of:
- Title and ownership (for example, ASIC extracts and the transfer instrument).
- Encumbrances (PPSR and other searches).
- Authority (board and shareholder approvals).

### 2.14 Other points
- **Mossvale (DD-009):** The assignment restriction does not state that consent is required merely because shares are sold. Confirm the position with the provision itself.
- **Office lease (DD-007):** Confirm whether landlord consent is required, not just a notification obligation.
- **"Negotiated positions":** Our response letter should state that nothing is agreed, that all positions remain subject to contract and playbook review, and that no concession is made by reason of the Seller's characterisation.

## 3. Summary of Recommendations

1. **Reject the Seller package as a basis for negotiation.** Respond that nothing is agreed and that all positions are subject to contract.
2. **Restore the general regime to playbook:** 25% / AUD 6m cap; AUD 5,000 de minimis; AUD 50,000 first-dollar basket; 24-month period. Do not offer the 20% or 18-month fallbacks without Amelia Frost's written authority identifying the draft.
3. **Separate Title and Fundamental claims:** 100% cap, at least six years, outside the basket, de minimis and knowledge bar. Reject the spillover clause.
4. **Carve out fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct** from all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable. Non-waivable.
5. **Reject whole-data-room and public-register disclosure.** Require specific fair disclosure. Refresh the disclosure to a current cut-off with bring-down.
6. **Delete the blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion** (cl 8.3). Any qualifier needs named seller knowledge persons and reasonable enquiry, and never applies to title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities.
7. **Bluefen:** Require effective written consent and evidence that conditions are satisfied before Completion. Reject consent-on-delivery and endeavours-only.
8. **Riverlark:** Require a current payout letter, direct repayment from Completion funds and effective security releases. Any post-Completion release needs an irrevocable undertaking and Frost approval.
9. **DD-005 bonuses:** Add AUD 420,000 plus quantified on-costs as a specific funds-flow line item or seller-funded. No silent exclusion.
10. **Ironquay:** Broaden the indemnity beyond SOW3 payment, preserve the SOW3 cure, and do not treat the AUD 180,000 as verified either way.
11. **DD-006:** Require log preservation, investigation and regular updates. Do not assume a breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand. Seek privacy counsel advice on whether any specific protection is needed.
12. **Sandbar renewals:** Request contracts and a breakdown. Assess without automatic debt classification or price deduction.
13. **Tax and IP:** Keep open. Reject the "settled" characterisation. Assume no unlimited liability and no resolution.
14. **Title:** Require independent title, ownership, encumbrance and authority evidence. DD-012 is not sufficient on its own.
15. **Confirm Mossvale and lease consent requirements** from the underlying provisions.

Before any response goes to the Seller, NSW counsel should confirm the drafting and the statutory points (particularly fraud carve-outs, Privacy Act exposure and enforceability of the limitation provisions).

The Seller calls these ordinary-course costs. The disclosure says it is unknown whether each renewal is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary-course. Request the contracts and a breakdown of each renewal. Do not accept the characterisation as settled, and do not automatically treat the amount as debt or deduct it from price. Keep the question open for the debt and working capital analysis.

### 2.12 Tax and IP
The Seller calls these "settled under the general regime." They are not. Our position is that Tax and IP terms remain open, with no unlimited liability and no resolution assumed. Keep Tax, IP, payment and covenant categories separate. Do not allow the general regime to override them quietly.

### 2.13 Title evidence
The share register at DD-012 is a Seller-supplied internal document, not independent proof. Require independent evidence of:
- Title and ownership (for example, ASIC extracts and the transfer instrument).
- Encumbrances (PPSR and other searches).
- Authority (board and shareholder approvals).

### 2.14 Other points
- **Mossvale (DD-009):** The assignment restriction does not state that consent is required merely because shares are sold. Confirm the position with the provision itself.
- **Office lease (DD-007):** Confirm whether landlord consent is required, not just a notification obligation.
- **"Negotiated positions":** Our response letter should state that nothing is agreed, that all positions remain subject to contract and playbook review, and that no concession is made by reason of the Seller's characterisation.

## 3. Summary of Recommendations

1. **Reject the Seller package as a basis for negotiation.** Respond that nothing is agreed and that all positions are subject to contract.
2. **Restore the general regime to playbook:** 25% / AUD 6m cap; AUD 5,000 de minimis; AUD 50,000 first-dollar basket; 24-month period. Do not offer the 20% or 18-month fallbacks without Amelia Frost's written authority identifying the draft.
3. **Separate Title and Fundamental claims:** 100% cap, at least six years, outside the basket, de minimis and knowledge bar. Reject the spillover clause.
4. **Carve out fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct** from all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable. Non-waivable.
5. **Reject whole-data-room and public-register disclosure.** Require specific fair disclosure. Refresh the disclosure to a current cut-off with bring-down.
6. **Delete the blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion** (cl 8.3). Any qualifier needs named seller knowledge persons and reasonable enquiry, and never applies to title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities.
7. **Bluefen:** Require effective written consent and evidence that conditions are satisfied before Completion. Reject consent-on-delivery and endeavours-only.
8. **Riverlark:** Require a current payout letter, direct repayment from Completion funds and effective security releases. Any post-Completion release needs an irrevocable undertaking and Frost approval.
9. **DD-005 bonuses:** Add AUD 420,000 plus quantified on-costs as a specific funds-flow line item or seller-funded. No silent exclusion.
10. **Ironquay:** Broaden the indemnity beyond SOW3 payment, preserve the SOW3 cure, and do not treat the AUD 180,000 as verified either way.
11. **DD-006:** Require log preservation, investigation and regular updates. Do not assume a breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand. Seek privacy counsel advice on whether any specific protection is needed.
12. **Sandbar renewals:** Request contracts and a breakdown. Assess without automatic debt classification or price deduction.
13. **Tax and IP:** Keep open. Reject the "settled" characterisation. Assume no unlimited liability and no resolution.
14. **Title:** Require independent title, ownership, encumbrance and authority evidence. DD-012 is not sufficient on its own.
15. **Confirm Mossvale and lease consent requirements** from the underlying provisions.

Before any response goes to the Seller, NSW counsel should confirm the drafting and the statutory points (particularly fraud carve-outs, Privacy Act exposure and enforceability of the limitation provisions).
